summary_md: **恒星sun ([@vintcessun](https://x.com/vintcessun/status/2116556308078059765))** explains *Small agents should know what their tools do* by Kovalenko and Redchych ([arXiv 2610.35981](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35981)): **EffectWorld** declares each tool's side effects, idempotency and resources so a replay verifier can judge safety; fine-tuning Qwen3-4B raised in-distribution success from 53% to 99% and held-out from 52% to 81% with about two-thirds fewer output tokens.

referenced_urls.title: Small agents should know what their tools do

relevance: Teaching small models tool side effects.

media.description: EffectWorld results table comparing base, SFT variants, unlikelihood, NPO and DPO on program/stepwise success, unconfirmed destructive calls, and BFCL accuracy.
EffectWorld examples of effect-safe tool use versus violations: unconfirmed destructive delete, duplicate non-idempotent email send, and stale-state write.
